title: Assembly of adjacent pushforward identifications
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, and $H$ a coherent formal module on $(X,\mathcal J)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], with underlying inverse system $H_\bullet$. Let $(T_n)_{n\ge0}$ be schemes with morphisms $i_n:T_n\to T_{n+1}$ and $j_n:T_n\to X$, equalities $j_{n+1}\circ i_n=j_n$, and specified tensor-pullback/pushforward adjunctions [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $R$ be a coherent thickening system on $(T_\bullet,i_\bullet)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-thickening-system], and $P(R)$ its explicit pushforward inverse system [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-system-pushforward-functor]. Write $p_n:P(R)_{n+1}\to P(R)_n$ and $h_n:H_{n+1}\to H_n$ for the adjacent transitions. Given isomorphisms $e_n:P(R)_n\xrightarrow{\sim}H_n$ with $e_n\circ p_n=h_n\circ e_{n+1}$ for all $n\ge0$, there is an isomorphism of inverse systems $P(R)\cong H_\bullet$ [def-weil-inverse-system], whose components are $e_n$. Here the positive indexing in the formal-module and inverse-system definitions is reindexed by $n\mapsto n+1$.

proof.text: Put $F=P(R)$ and $G=H_\bullet$. The pushforward-functor statement supplies $F$ as an inverse system. A coherent formal module has an underlying inverse system $G$. Reindex the inverse-system definition from positive integers to $n\ge0$. By that definition a morphism of inverse systems is precisely a component family commuting with adjacent transitions. Hence the given equations define a morphism $e:F\to G$ with components $e_n$. In the functor presentation, compatibility with a transition $m\to n$ follows by induction on $m-n$: the case $m=n$ is the identity equation; composing the equation for $m\to n$ with the adjacent equation for $m+1\to m$ gives the equation for $m+1\to n$ by associativity.

source.place: Remark 088F (remark-reformulate-existence-theorem), formal assembly of the systems; equation 0880 (equation-completion-functor)

proof.text: Let $d_n=e_n^{-1}:G_n\to F_n$. Compose $e_n\circ p_n=h_n\circ e_{n+1}$ on the left with $d_n$ and on the right with $d_{n+1}$. The inverse identities and associativity give $p_n\circ d_{n+1}=d_n\circ h_n$. Thus the inverse-system morphism definition gives a morphism $d:G\to F$ with components $d_n$. Explicitly, write $p_{m,n}:F_m\to F_n$ and $h_{m,n}:G_m\to G_n$ for the composites of adjacent transitions. For $m=n$, $p_{n,n}\circ d_n=d_n\circ h_{n,n}$ is the identity law. If $p_{m,n}\circ d_m=d_n\circ h_{m,n}$, then $p_{m+1,n}\circ d_{m+1}=p_{m,n}\circ p_m\circ d_{m+1}=p_{m,n}\circ d_m\circ h_m=d_n\circ h_{m,n}\circ h_m=d_n\circ h_{m+1,n}$. This proves compatibility with every transition by induction on $m-n$.

source.place: Remark 088F (remark-reformulate-existence-theorem), formal assembly of the systems; equation 0880 (equation-completion-functor)

proof.text: Composition of inverse-system morphisms is componentwise. At every $n$, $(d\circ e)_n=d_n\circ e_n=\mathrm{id}_{F_n}$ and $(e\circ d)_n=e_n\circ d_n=\mathrm{id}_{G_n}$. Equality of component families therefore proves $d\circ e=\mathrm{id}_F$ and $e\circ d=\mathrm{id}_G$. The pair $(e,d)$ is the required isomorphism, with the prescribed components.
